entry.dc:title: PRODUCTIVITY IN THE NONFERROUS METALS INDUSTRY.
entry.dc:creator: Michal E.
entry.dc:description: Changes in productivity in the nonferrous metals industry have been both positive and negative. Open-pit mining operations show improved productivity, while capital-intensive milling, smelting, and refining operations show only slight improvements. Underground mining is retrogressing. The article discusses the major factors influencing productivity which are: labor management attitudes, capital investment, resource and energy availability, technological improvement, product quality requirements, and regulatory actions.

entry.dc:title: Technology of Crusher Utilization in Hard-Rock Open-Pit Mining in the German Democratic Republic.
entry.dc:creator: Strzodka K.
entry.dc:description: The use of stationary and mobile crushers in open-pit mining is discussed. The various types of mobile crushers used in the GDR are reviewed, and the equipment required for hard-rock open-pit mining with mobile crushers and belt conveyors is indicated. The results obtained from the use of these crushers are evaluated.

entry.dc:title: Development of Mining Work at Ekibastuz Deposit.
entry.dc:creator: Tynterov I.
entry.dc:description: The plan of 600m deep open-pit mining operations adapted at the initial stage of the development of the huge Ekibastuz deposit in Kazakhstan is criticized as having a number of essential shortcomings on particular deconcentration of mining operations and wrong choice of priority working sections. Some ways to correct the situation are considered.

entry.dc:title: QUEBRADA BLANCA, CHILE: AN ENRICHED PORPHYRY COPPER DEPOSIT.
entry.dc:creator: Hunt J.P.
entry.dc:description: The Quebrada Blanca copper/molybdenum prospect lies in the high Andes of Chile. The Superior Oil-Falconbridge Group began exploration in 1977 under a joint venture foreign investment agreement with the Chilean government. A successful exploration program has developed an open-pit mining reserve, provided samples for bulk metallurgical testing, and located supplies of water for future operations. The main orebody is amenable to conventional metallurgical treatment and contains more than 400 Mt (441 million st) of recoverable ore at about a 1:1 stripping ratio. The average millhead grade during the first six years of operations will exceed 1. 5% Cu, plus recoverable molybdenum values. Several hundred million tons of additional reserves are available.

entry.dc:title: BULLMOOSE MINE PROJECT.
entry.dc:creator: Drozd R.
entry.dc:description: The Bullmoose Mine is currently under construction in the north east coal area of British Columbia and approximately 300 million will be spent. This paper covers the history and exploration work on the property, the geology, open-pit mining plans and equipment, the preparation plant flowsheet from breaker station to clean coal silo, the 35 km highway truck haul, railroad loadout system, manpower requirements, construction progress, approvals and permits, and financial arrangements.

entry.dc:title: Recents Developments in Open-Pit Mining.
entry.dc:creator: Gurs P.
entry.dc:description: Spectacular progress has been made in open-pit mining during the last 20 years of industrial expansion, both from the point of view of technical advances in equipment and in mining and management methods. The purpose of the present article is to review the current trends in open-pit mining methods and equipment and to indicate some recent achievements and the size of equipment available for future projects.

entry.dc:title: OPTIMUM SCHEDULING OF OVERBURDEN REMOVAL IN OPEN-PIT MINES.
entry.dc:creator: Qing-Xia Yun
entry.dc:description: This paper formulates optimum production scheduling in open-pit mining as an inventory problem and develops a solution using dynamic programming techniques.

entry.dc:title: COST CONSIDERATIONS FOR IN-PIT CRUSHING/CONVEYING SYSTEMS.
entry.dc:creator: Huss C.
entry.dc:description: This article focuses on continuous materials handling systems used in the hard rock open-pit mining industry. Guidelines for mine planning with continuous systems are outlined. Key parameters affecting capital and operating costs are identified. Commonly encountered trade-offs between operating and capital costs are discussed. A typical range of costs is presented based on average operating conditions.

entry.dc:title: OPEN-PIT LIGNITE MINING IN SPAIN.
entry.dc:creator: Anon
entry.dc:description: The article discusses examples of solid-rock open-pit mining in the mining regions of Teruel Sur and Tereul Norte-Mequinenza, 90km south-south-west of Zaragoza.

entry.dc:title: MATERIALS MANAGEMENT AT BRENDA MINES LTD.
entry.dc:creator: Sperlins G.
entry.dc:description: Brenda Mines Ltd. is a low-grade open-pit mining and milling operation located near Peachland, B. C. The plane treats an average of 30,000 tons per day of an ore that contains 0. 130% copper and 0. 030% molybdenum. The objective of the materials management progam is to solve problems relating to materials from a total organization or system viewpoint.

entry.dc:title: DETERMINING THE OPTIMAL DEPTH OF AN OPEN PIT.
entry.dc:creator: Nilsson D.
entry.dc:description: To determine the optimal depth of an open pit, the Office of Surface Mining, US Department of the Interior, is sponsoring a research project at Michigan Technological University titled ″The effects of increasing energy costs on the future relation between open-pit and underground mining.″ This article analyzes the economic value of various pit depths for one hypothetical example from the project. The conclusion is that with a price of 5/ton of ore, the deposit can be mined with open pit methods down to a depth of 200 m, with future underground mining being unprofitable. With a price of 10/ton, open-pit mining can proceed down to a depth of 300 m. It would be more profitable, however, to change over to underground mining at 250 m depth.

entry.dc:title: DEVELOPING AND EVALUATING PIT TRUCK SAFETY DEVICES.
entry.dc:creator: Yates W.
entry.dc:description: Driver visibility is restricted in large, rear-dump haulage trucks used in open-pit mining. Analysis shows the need for an alarm to warn of vehicles in blind spots. Anaconda developed an electromagnetic system whereby smaller vehicles transmit a signal to haulage truck operators to alert them to their presence. The system has been field-tested at the Twin Buttes open-pit mine near Tucson, Ariz.

entry.dc:title: SIMULATED OPEN-PIT MINING CONDITIONS USED TO TEACH DRAGLINE OPERATORS.
entry.dc:creator: Eschman C.
entry.dc:description: The Dragline Training System uses a dragline simulator to provide a skills development program for training and retraining dragline operators.

entry.dc:title: SURFACE MINING - PAST, PRESENT AND FUTURE.
entry.dc:creator: Atkinson T.
entry.prism:publicationName: Journal of Mines Metals and Fuels
entry.dc:description: The article reviews the history, current state-of-the-art and future trends of development in the field of surface mining. The main topics discussed cover the limits of scale of surface mining operations performed by walking draglines and bucket wheel excavators; mine design and planning for strip, terrace and open-pit mining; ground preparation including drilling and blasting operations; loading and haulage equipment; and surface mine electric power systems.

entry.dc:title: Hydraulic excavators solve economic and operational problems in open-pit.
entry.dc:description: The use and servicing of hydraulic excavators in open-pit mining operations in France is discussed.

entry.dc:title: BUCIM COPPER PROJECT: YUGOSLAVIA'S NEW 85 MILLION MINE AND FLOTATION CONCENTRATOR WILL PRODUCE 100,000 MT/YR OF COPPER CONCENTRATE.
entry.dc:creator: Westergard A.
entry.dc:description: The Bucim Copper Project in Yugoslavia, in operation since mid 1979, uses conventional open-pit mining and ore processing methods and includes some of the largest mining and processing equipment in the world. After a historical summary, the article deals with ore genesis, the process design criteria, mining and crushing, grinding and flotation, filtration and tails handling, and instrumentation.

entry.dc:title: Public policy for the management of groundwater in the coastal plains of North Carolina.
entry.dc:creator: Sherwani J.
entry.dc:description: The need for management is emphasized by the fact that in some parts of the region, the aquifer system is reaching its production potential to permit open-pit mining for phosphate ore. The areas of large concentrated withdrawals and extensive lowering of the potentiometric surface have created conditions for possible water quality deterioration. The projections of water needs for municipal, industrial, and agricultural uses to the year 2000 are developed. -from US Govt Reports Announcements, 24, 1980

entry.dc:title: Costs of Learning about the Environmental Damage of Mining Projects
entry.dc:creator: CAMPBELL H.
entry.dc:description: Two ways of gathering information about and mitigating the impact of a large‐scale mining project are briefly described and contrasted:one way involves postponing the construction and operation of the project while attempts are made to forecast, evaluate and prepare for its impact; the other way involves commencing immediately with a small‐scale, or attenuated, project with a smaller impact and by studying the effects of this project inferring the impact of a large‐scale project. The costs of the two alternative policies of postponement and attenuation are defied as reductions m the present value of the project in question. A model of open‐pit mining is perished which allows these costs to be calculated for any degree of postponement or attenuation. The model is applied to three uranium mines in the Northern Territory of Australia to estimate for each mine the costs of the two policies. The model is then used to estimate the costs of sequences of mine development in the Northern Territory involving various combinations of postponement and attenuation policies. The costs of these policies are then compared with the reduction in the impact of the industry using the population of a mining town site as a proxy for impact. This comparison is a first step towards a benefit/cost analysis of the two policies. Copyright © 1980, Wiley Blackwell. All rights reserved

entry.dc:title: Economic evaluation of the damage caused to natural and economic features by the iron-ore industry of the KMA.
entry.dc:creator: Forafontova V.I.
entry.dc:description: The growing iron-ore industry of the Kursk Magnetic Anomaly in central Russia causes heavy damage to the environment because of heavy reliance on open-pit operations. The damage includes the transfer of fertile chernozem farmland to mining uses, the razing of settlements and the need for resettling the displaced population, the transfer of land in industry to mining uses, and the cost of restoring the regional water-management balance after disruption by open-pit mining. Formulas for calculating the replacement cost of the disrupted features are proposed, and the resulting reduction of the cost-effectiveness of the mining operations is calculated. The transfer of farmland to nonfarm uses is found to be the greatest factor reducing the cost-effectiveness of the mining operations. The restoration of the water balance is less of a factor, and the compensation for the razing of settlement and industry is found to be negligible, possibly because some aspects were not considered in the calculations.- from Soviet Geography

entry.dc:title: Kyanite mining in Virginia.
entry.dc:creator: Dixon G.
entry.dc:description: Reserves of kyanite in Buckingham County, Virginia, will last several decades, especially at the open-pit mining operation at Willis Mountain. This short review considers the history, mining, processing, and economic uses of kyanite. -R.S.M.

entry.dc:title: HOW BLASTHOLE SHOCK ABSORBERS REDUCE COSTS.
entry.dc:creator: Work J.
entry.dc:description: Spiraling costs in every segment of the open-pit mining cycle is a fact of life that every operator must reckon with. The introduction of various shock absorbing devices for rotary drilling is one recent innovation that may significantly reduce overall drilling cost, increase drill availability, and lower maintenance requirements. A shock absorber is simply a device installed between the rotary drive head and drill steel that cushions the two. It functions in the same manner as springs and shocks on an automobile. The article discusses benefits of shock absorbers, including minimizing vibrations, extending bit life, and lowering maintenance needs.

entry.dc:title: FIELD TESTING AND EVALUATION OF SERVICE BRAKE CAPABILITY FOR LARGE-SIZE DIESEL-ELECTRIC HAULAGE TRUCKS.
entry.dc:creator: Sahay H.
entry.dc:description: This paper describes the main testing procedures that should be carried out to evaluate the capacity and capability of the service brakes on the large-size diesel-electric trucks now in common use at open-pit mining operations. Brake testing programs in general are described, then consideration is given to different techniques of service brake testing, brake performance evaluation, braking energy and typical performance characteristics.

entry.dc:title: QUINSAM COAL PROJECT.
entry.dc:creator: Barnstable D.
entry.dc:description: Quinsam Coal Ltd. is assessing the potential of developing a thermal coal deposit near Middle Quinsam Lake on Vancouver Island in British Columbia, Canada. The coal reserve outlined is classified as a high-volatile, bituminous ″A″ steam coal and is composed of four separate seams of varying quality within the Late Cretaceous Comox Formation. Open-pit mining methods will utilize a walking dragline and a truck/shovel module as the primary stripping tools. Following washing and mechanical drying in a Baum jig preparation plant, the coal will be transported to the proposed dock at Campbell River for shipment via 55,000-DWT vessels to world markets. The paper outlines the development and status of the project to date.

entry.dc:title: ANALYSIS OF EQUIPMENT REQUIREMENTS FOR ANTHRACITE OPEN-PIT MINING.
entry.dc:creator: Manula C.V.
entry.dc:description: The Mineral Engineering Department of The Pennsylvania State University has developed a suite of computer models for anthracite open pit mining. Individual subsystems have been developed to (a) interpolate geologic field data to obtain coal tonnages, waste volumes, and strip ratios; (b) simulate equipment performance on selected pit profiles to generate data required to choose coal and waste removal equipment; and (c) evaluate selected cost factors to determine either a rate of return for a specified selling price or vice-versa. This paper describes the application of two of these subsystems, namely the Reserves Model (GEOL) and the Open Pit Materials Handlng Simulator (OPMHS), and how these may be applied for the selection of equipment for a prime anthracite mining site.

entry.dc:title: Geology of the Athabasca oil sands
entry.dc:creator: Mossop G.D.
entry.dc:description: In-place bitumen resources in the Alberta oil sands are estimated at 1350 billion barrels. Open-pit mining and hot water extraction methods, which involve the handling of huge tonnages of earth materials, are being employed in the two commercial plants now operating. In situ recovery methods will be required to tap the 90 percent of reserves that are too deeply buried to be surface mined. Development of in situ technologies will be painstaking and expensive, and success will hinge on their compatibility with extremely complex geological conditions in the subsurface.
